question: How much funding has been pledged and actually disbursed to Ukraine by the European Union and each Member State since February 2022, including military, financial, humanitarian and economic support? What costs have been incurred as a result of accommodating and assisting Ukrainian refugees?

Does the Commission know how much Member States have paid Russia in the same period to import energy (all forms of energy and transport charges)? The Commission is asked to provide the total amount and, if possible, the amounts broken down by Member State.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (5.11.2026) As of mid-October 2026, the EU and its Member States have enabled the mobilisation of EUR 231.5 billion in total since 20221. At the same time, the EU has taken decisive steps to end its historic dependence on Russian fossil fuels and deprive Russia of energy revenues. EU purchases of Russian fossil fuels have fallen sharply since the Russian invasion of Ukraine.

The EU has stopped purchasing Russian coal in August 2022 and has banned new purchases of Russian refined oil products in February 2023. In December 2025, the EU agreed on a gradual but permanent stop of Russian gas imports and phase out of Russian oil2.

As a result, payments for Russian fossil fuels fell to EUR 17 billion in 2025, representing only 5% of the EU’s total fossil-fuel imports and almost 90% less than the EUR 144 billion paid in 2022. Between January 2022 and December 2025, the EU paid EUR 213 billion for Russian fossil fuels, reflecting, in particular, the EU’s pre-existing energy dependence.

These payments decreased significantly over the period, in line with the EU’s efforts to diversify its energy supplies and progressively phase out imports of Russian fossil fuels. These commercial transactions are distinct in nature from the EU’s financial, military and humanitarian support to Ukraine.
